decision: gh copilot (the GitHub CLI extension) cannot be used as an LLM provider — it only supports shell command suggest/explain and returns 403 on chat API calls. The standalone copilot binary (shipped with VS Code Copilot Chat extension) supports -p/--prompt and is the correct integration point.
key_insight: gh copilot (the GitHub CLI extension) cannot be used as an LLM provider — it only supports shell command suggest/explain and returns 403 on chat API calls. The standalone copilot binary (shipped with VS Code Copilot Chat extension) supports -p/--prompt and is the correct integration point.
alternatives_considered: Use gh copilot suggest/explain as a roundabout LLM proxy
Use the GitHub Copilot REST API directly with a token
rejected_reason: gh copilot is limited to shell command generation — calling the chat endpoint returns 403 (integration does not have GitHub chat enabled)
The GitHub Copilot REST API requires a specific token scope that gh auth does not provide by default
notes: gh copilot is installed via: gh extension install github/gh-copilot (tested v1.1.1)
The standalone copilot binary lives at: ~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/globalStorage/github.copilot-chat/copilotCli/copilot
The copilot binary is a shell wrapper that runs VS Code Electron node with copilotCLIShim.js
Auth probe: ~/.copilot/session-state/ has at least one UUID directory after first sign-in
Usage: copilot -p '<prompt>' --output-format json  ->  JSONL stream, extract assistant.message event
The copilot binary is added to PATH automatically by VS Code when the Copilot Chat extension is installed
